title: Animation Track Property Type does not correspond with Keyframe's value type in the case of subproperties (eg: Vector3.x, Color.r)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot v4.1 and Godot v4.1.1.


### System information

Windows 10 - Godot v4.1.1stable

### Issue description

When making an animation, if on a track I specify a subproperty from a vector3 for example (eg. `position:x`), the keyframes all turn into Xs because there's a type mismatch between the keyframe value types and the track property type.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cd447b6-cf61-4ee3-b25d-d4c1aa5d9993)

This used to work on previous versions of Godot, but now it doesn't work anymore for some reason...

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a scene.
- Add a node in the scene (that should have a vector3 or vector2 property like, for example, position)
- Add an AnimationPlayer, create an animation.
- Add a new animation track, select the added node, and in the position property (or any vector property, even Color property doesn't work) click on the dropdown icon on the left and select a component from the vector. You should now have a track with the property position:x for example.
- Add a keyframe to the track. If you click on that keyframe and check the AnimationTrackKeyEdit inspector of it, you will notice that the type of the value mismatches the type of the property. Try to modify the value of the keyframe and it'll turn into a red cross.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

MRP on Godot v4.1.1

[keyframetypemismatch.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20967957/keyframetypemismatch.zip)
